en: The train that comes from South Africa

The train that comes from South Africa
notes: Shosholoza is left as it stands: it is a call to push on, move forward together (from a verb for sliding or pushing forward), often heard as imitating the sound of the steam train; it has no single English word.
line 1.3 etc.: 'Kulezo ntaba' is 'on (from, in) those mountains'; the locative can mean any of these.

line 1.4 etc.: 'Stimela' is the train (from English 'steam'); 'siphume' is read as 'that comes / came out of'. Other versions of the song name Rhodesia or Zimbabwe instead of South Africa: it was sung by migrant workers travelling to and from the mines.
line 1.8: 'Wen' uyabaleka' is 'You are running (away)'; 'ukubaleka' can mean to run or to flee.
